newsitem.title: TURKEY: Iraqi Kurd group rejects Baghdad mediation offer.
newsitem.headline: Iraqi Kurd group rejects Baghdad mediation offer.

text.p: An Iraqi Kurdish group on Tuesday rejected Baghdad's offer to mediate between warring Kurdish factions in northern Iraq and said any resolution to the crisis would require an American diplomatic and military role.
Adnan Mufti, a senior official in the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), also repeated assurances the group had received no military backing from neighbouring Iran.
"We do not believe in Baghdad's policy, but we are asking for the continuation of U.S. mediation," Mufti told Reuters. He was in Ankara for meetings with Turkish and U.S diplomats.

Mufti said the PUK demanded the continuation of American humanitarian aid and protection for Iraqi Kurds under Operation Provide Comfort, the U.S.-led air force patrolling northern Iraq from a base in Turkey since shortly after the 1991 Gulf war.

Iraqi leaders on Sunday urged both factions to put aside their differences and resume dialogue with Baghdad after the PUK recaptured Sulaimaniya, which it lost to the rival Kurdistan Democratic Party (KDP) last month.
But Mufti said the KDP must first cut its recent ties to the central government in Baghdad before any settlement was possible.

"We are asking to have peace for our people and good relations between the PUK and the KDP. But for that, the KDP must stop its connections with Baghdad to have a chance to talk about our future," he said.
KDP leader Massoud Barzani, who cut a deal in August with Baghdad to secure control of the north, on Sunday accused Iranian forces of entering northern Iraq on the side of the rival PUK.
"They must prove their allegation. Everybody saw on television Iraqi tanks which supported KDP peshmergas (guerrillas) in early clashes, but nobody has see any Iranian involvement," Mufti said.
